scope: Nineteen complete public cards read; SOIS-240 from the same final20 allocation is separately integrated. Manual review is not runtime evidence or completeness certification.

IGME-382.name: Maps, Mapping and Geospatial Technologies
IGME-382.description: Surveys ways to represent the Earth using GPS, GIS, remote sensing, virtual globes and mapping mashups, developing spatial reasoning through practical work.

category_review.locator: IGME-382 link and complete IGME-382 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The organizing content is geospatial representation and use of geographic tools, not a general computing curriculum.

IGME-384.name: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
IGME-384.description: Develops geographic research projects using spatial data models, cartography, geodatabases, data acquisition and spatial analysis; considers geographic problems and data ethics.

category_review.locator: IGME-384 link and complete IGME-384 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Spatial problem solving and applied geographic research organize the database and visualization tools.

IGME-386.name: Spatial Algorithms and Problem Solving
IGME-386.description: Compares spatial algorithms and develops computer implementations to solve spatial problems and build computational reasoning.
IGME-386.prerequisites: This class is restricted to undergraduate students with at least 2nd year standing.

category_review.locator: IGME-386 link and complete IGME-386 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The description centers algorithm comparison, encoding and implementation rather than merely using geographic software.

IGME-484.name: Geographic Visualization
IGME-484.description: Examines mapping theory, comprehension, evaluation and construction, including three-dimensional and animated maps, through a geographic research project.
IGME-484.prerequisites: This class is restricted to undergraduate students with at least 3rd year standing.

category_review.locator: IGME-484 link and complete IGME-484 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Cartography and geographic visualization practice are the primary domain.

IGME-489.name: Geospatial Artificial Intelligence
IGME-489.description: Applies language models, natural-language geocoding, model APIs, neural networks, raster analysis and predictive models to geographic problems, with programming projects and discussion of bias and privacy.
IGME-489.prerequisites: Prerequisites: GCIS-124 or CSCI-140 or CSCI-142 or CSCI-242 or ISTE-200 or IGME-201 or IGME-106 or GCIS-127 or equivalent course or AISYS-MN or GIS-MN or GIS-IM students.
notes: The prerequisite explicitly includes declared GIS-IM students as an alternative; no additional prerequisite chain is invented.

category_review.locator: IGME-489 link and complete IGME-489 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The actual description explicitly teaches language-model and neural-network methods for spatial analysis.

ISCH-370.name: Principles Of Data Science
ISCH-370.description: Covers acquisition and preparation of data, exploratory analysis, statistical and machine-learning methods, visualization, ethical concerns and a communicated analysis project.
ISCH-370.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CSCI-101 or ISCH-110 or equivalent course. No GCCIS students can take this course for credit toward their degree requirement.
notes: The body separately says GCCIS majors may enroll only with home-department approval and may not apply these credits toward degree requirements. Permission to enroll does not remove the credit prohibition.

category_review.locator: ISCH-370 link and complete ISCH-370 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The source substantially combines statistical inference and machine-learning methods without establishing one primary taxonomy subject.

STAT-145.name: Introduction to Statistics I
STAT-145.description: Introduces exploratory data analysis, data integrity, sampling distributions, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests, emphasizing statistical reasoning with software.
STAT-145.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Any 100 level MATH course, or NMTH-260 or NMTH-272 or NMTH-275 or (NMTH-250 with a C- or better) or a Math Placement Exam score of at least 35.

category_review.locator: STAT-145 link and complete STAT-145 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Statistical inference and reasoning are the explicit core content.

DHSS-488.name: Special Topics
DHSS-488.description: Examines a selected digital-humanities topic through critical study and practical work; general-education use requires approval where applicable.
notes: The route requires Topic ID #4, Humanitarian Free & Open Source Software Development. This generic Special Topics card does not independently supply that offering-specific description; other topics are not automatically eligible.

category_review.locator: DHSS-488 link and complete DHSS-488 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The actual generic card does not describe the specific Topic ID #4 software-development offering required by this route; a definite primary subject is not certified from this generic body.

ISCH-201.name: Computing, Culture and Society
ISCH-201.description: Examines computing history and ethics through privacy, speech, intellectual property, work, inequality, algorithmic bias, environmental issues and public debate.
ISCH-201.prerequisites: Computing majors may take this course only with department approval.
notes: This eligibility statement appears in the body; no formal prerequisite field is printed. No degree-credit prohibition is stated here, unlike ISCH-370.

category_review.locator: ISCH-201 link and complete ISCH-201 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Ethical and social interpretation of computing, papers and debate organize the course.

DHSS-377.name: Media Narrative
DHSS-377.description: Analyzes linear, nonlinear and interactive narrative across traditional and digital media, developing critical interpretation and a final media project.

category_review.locator: DHSS-377 link and complete DHSS-377 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The stated focus is critical analysis of media narrative; the source describes practical implementation as minimal, supporting the primary communication/cultural purpose.

DHSS/ITDL-500.name: Transmedia Storytelling
DHSS/ITDL-500.description: Studies the theory, practice and ethics of stories across platforms; students analyze narrative aesthetics and create a transmedia story while considering audience engagement, copyright and responsible technology use.
notes: The literal DHSS/ITDL-500 menu link opens actual DHSS-500. This observation does not certify an additional ITDL alias or a second requirement.

category_review.locator: DHSS/ITDL-500 link and complete DHSS-500 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Narrative communication, aesthetic interpretation and ethical storytelling are the primary content; production tools support that purpose.

ITDL-151H.name: Explorations of Place and Space
ITDL-151H.description: Uses an experiential honors seminar to investigate how social worlds relate to natural and built environments through inquiry, interpretation and a selected theme.
ITDL-151H.prerequisites: This class is restricted to students in the Honors program.
notes: The seminar integrates the required Year One curriculum; the instructor-selected topic is announced separately.

category_review.locator: ITDL-151H link and complete ITDL-151H public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The description emphasizes interpretation of the human condition and social relationships to place.

ITDL-205.name: Grand Challenges: Clean Water
ITDL-205.description: Uses interdisciplinary teams, case studies and analysis of social and technical constraints to propose sustainable responses to clean-water access problems.
ITDL-205.prerequisites: Prerequisites: This class is restricted to students with 1st or 2nd year standing.

category_review.locator: ITDL-205 link and complete ITDL-205 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The organizing task is applied clean-water problem solving and alternative solutions, informed by social context rather than solely cultural interpretation.

UWRT-365.name: Writing, Public Speaking and Civic Engagement
UWRT-365.description: Develops rhetorical analysis, writing, presentations and revision through investigation of public concerns, social justice and civic organizations.

category_review.locator: UWRT-365 link and complete UWRT-365 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Writing, public speaking, rhetoric and civic interpretation are explicitly central.

ITDL-211.name: Vertically Integrated Projects GE
ITDL-211.description: Conducts sustained collaborative liberal-arts and sciences research on a faculty-led interdisciplinary project, using disciplinary methods and analytical frameworks.
notes: Published range is 1–3 credits; three research contact hours are not a scalar credit amount.
The immersion requires all nine credits on the same project, at least three through ITDL-511; permission applies to every registration.

category_review.locator: ITDL-211 link and complete ITDL-211 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The description expressly permits humanities, social-science and natural-science inquiry without naming a specific project; no single primary subject is established.

ITDL-511.name: Vertically Integrated Projects GE
ITDL-511.description: Conducts sustained collaborative liberal-arts and sciences research on a faculty-led interdisciplinary project, using disciplinary methods and analytical frameworks. Advanced students also mentor team members and help guide intellectual direction.
notes: Published range is 1–3 credits; three research contact hours are not a scalar credit amount.
The immersion requires all nine credits on the same project, at least three through ITDL-511; permission applies to every registration.

category_review.locator: ITDL-511 link and complete ITDL-511 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The description expressly permits humanities, social-science and natural-science inquiry without naming a specific project; no single primary subject is established.

ISCH-110.name: Principles of Computing
ISCH-110.description: Introduces computational ideas through step-by-step problem solving and programming, with individual and team work and discussion of computing in daily life.
ISCH-110.prerequisites: Computer Science majors may take this course only with department approval, and may not apply these credits toward their degree requirements.
notes: The body names Computer Science majors; it is not silently broadened to all GCCIS degrees. The whole Principles of Computing route separately requires ISCH-370, whose GCCIS-wide credit prohibition is explicit.

category_review.locator: ISCH-110 link and complete ISCH-110 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Algorithmic problem formulation and implementation in a programming language establish the primary introductory computing content.

SOCI/ANTH-246.name: Gender and Health
SOCI/ANTH-246.description: Examines gender differences in health outcomes, reproductive rights, HIV/AIDS, violence, global trends and health-care inequities and policy.
notes: The literal SOCI/ANTH-246 link opens actual SOCI-246; no separate ANTH alias is certified.

category_review.locator: SOCI/ANTH-246 link and complete SOCI-246 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: The course interprets gender inequalities and social policy through health case studies, rather than teaching clinical practice.

PRFL/WGST-330.name: Performing Identity in Popular Media
PRFL/WGST-330.description: Examines the construction and performance of personal identity and diversity in popular media through theory, readings, film and critical writing.
notes: The literal PRFL/WGST-330 link opens actual PRFL-330; no separate WGST alias is certified.

category_review.locator: PRFL/WGST-330 link and complete PRFL-330 public card, 2026–2027 route
category_review.rationale: Critical interpretation of identity politics and cultural representation is the stated organizing work, not a studio-performance curriculum.
